name: 3% saline
Dose: Oral (neonate practice): 0.5-1mL per feed (2-6mmol/kg/day). 1mL = 0.513mmol Na. IV for severe (<120mmol/L) or symptomatic hyponatraemia: 3-5mL/kg over 15 minutes (raises Na by 2.5-4mmol/L). Deficit (mmol) = (target Na - current Na) x 0.6 (male) or 0.5 (female) x weight. Overly rapid correction can cause osmotic demyelination.
Incompatibilities: Fat emulsion
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Uptodate

name: Acetazolamide 250mg Tablet
Dose: 5-10mg/kg BD-QID TB hydrocephalus: 25-50mg/kg TDS-QID, usual dose: 100mg/kg/day (in divided doses)
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Strength of EXTEMP prep: 25mg/mL

name: Acetylcysteine 200mg/ml Injection [NAC]
Dose: Paracetamol poisoning, <20kg: Step 1 200mg/kg in 7ml/kg D5% over 4 hours; Step 2 100mg/kg in 14ml/kg D5% over 16 hours (repeat Step 2 if indicated). Send paracetamol level. Non-paracetamol acute liver failure: Step 1 150mg/kg in 50ml D5% over 2 hours; Step 2 150mg/kg in 50ml D5% over 24 hours (repeat if indicated). Use NS if D5% unsuitable.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Paed Protocol 5th edition

name: Acetylsalicylic acid/ (Aspirin) 300mg tablet
Dose: Anti-platelet: 3-5mg/kg/dose OD (serve after feeding). Kawasaki disease (acute): 30-50mg/kg/day in 3-4 divided doses.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Freshly prepare, ensure well mixing, watchout for sedimentation.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: UpToDate

name: Aciclovir 200mg tablet (oral)
Dose: HSV/herpes zoster/varicella - infants & children: 20mg/kg/dose QID for 5-7 days [Max 800mg/dose]. HSV post-exposure prophylaxis: 20mg/kg/dose QID for 7 days. Ideal body weight if obese (AKI risk).
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026

name: Aciclovir 250mg injection
Dose: HSV infection: ≤3 months 20mg/kg 8 hourly; >3 months-12 years 10-15mg/kg/dose 8 hourly. Duration 7-14 days for mucocutaneous disease; at least 21 days for CNS/disseminated infection. Perinatally acquired varicella: prophylaxis 15mg/kg/dose 8 hourly for 5 days (mother developed varicella 5 days before to 2 days after delivery, OR when VZIG not available - use with IVIG); treatment 15mg/kg 8 hourly for 7-10 days. Herpes zoster/varicella (infants & children): 10mg/kg/dose 8 hourly. Note: weight-based dosing (ideal body weight if obese) preferred over BSA because of high risk of acute kidney injury.
Incompatibilities: Fat emulsion, aztreonam, caffeine citrate, caspofungin, cefepime, dobutamine, dopamine, meropenem, piperacillin-tazobactam
Storage after reconstitution: 12-24h depending on brand, do not refrigerate
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: NeoFax 2020

name: Actrapid 1000 iu/10ml (Insulin) injection
Dose: NICU/SCN insulin infusion (sliding scale): full strength 2 units/kg in 20ml NS (1ml/H = 0.1unit/kg/hr); half strength 1 unit/kg in 20ml (1ml/H = 0.05unit/kg/hr); quarter strength 0.5 unit/kg in 20ml (1ml/H = 0.025unit/kg/hr). Preparation: draw 0.2ml (20 IU) Actrapid + 19.8ml NS = 1 IU/ml, then draw prescribed amount and make up to 20ml with NS. Sliding scale rate by DXT (mmol/L): >18 1ml/hr; >16-18 0.9; >14-16 0.8; >12-14 0.7; >10-12 0.5; >8-10 0.3; >6-8 0.1ml/hr. Hyperkalaemia: urgent 0.1 IU/kg in 5mL/kg D10% over 30 min; non-urgent 0.05-0.1 IU/kg in 5mL/kg D10% over 1 hour with DXT monitoring (see Hyperkalaemia tab). Stable 24h after dilution; vial 6 weeks after opening.
Incompatibilities: Cefoperazone, Diazepam, Ketamine, Micafungin, Phenytoin, Tazocin, Polymyxin B, Protamine sulphate, Rocuronium, Bactrim
Method of administration: Hyperglycemia: continuous infusion. Hyperkalemia: infusion over 1 hour.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Starship Newborn Intensive Care, KEMH

name: Adenosine 6mg/2ml injection
Dose: 1st dose 0.1mg/kg/dose. If no response within 2 min, give 2nd dose 0.2mg/kg/dose. If no response, give 3rd dose 0.3mg/kg/dose. Max 0.3mg/kg/dose.
Incompatibilities: Single line, do not mix with other medications
Method of administration: IV push over 1-2 sec followed by rapid NS flush via 3-way tap, prefer upper limb close to heart
Ref: ANMF, NeoFax

name: Adrenaline 1mg/1ml (1:1000) injection
Dose: Cardiac arrest: IV 0.2ml/kg of 1:10,000 (0.01-0.03mg/kg). ET: 1mL/kg of 1:10,000. Anaphylaxis IM: 0.01mg/kg/dose (max 0.3mg). Continuous infusion (MGH): peripheral 0.15mg/kg in 50ml NS/D5% (1ml/hr = 0.05mcg/kg/min, max 30ml/hr = 1.5mcg/kg/min); central 0.3mg/kg in 50ml (1ml/hr = 0.1mcg/kg/min, max 15ml/hr = 1.5mcg/kg/min). Nebulised (croup/stridor, MGH): 0.5ml/kg of pure 1mg/ml [Max 4ml], add NS up to total 4ml.
Incompatibilities: Aminophylline, Ampicillin, Micafungin, Omeprazole, Sodium bicarbonate, Thiopenthal
Method of administration: Rapid push+3ml saline flush, or ETT, or continuous infusion, or nebulisation
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Leaflet, UpToDate, NeoFax

name: Alphacalcidol drops 2 mcg/ml
Dose: Neonate: 0.1mcg/kg OD. Infant & child <20kg: 0.05mcg/kg OD (adjust to response/ease of administration). 1 drop = 0.1mcg.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Product insert

name: Alprostadil 500mcg/ml injection (Prostin)
Dose: Maintain patency of ductus arteriosus: starting dose 10-40ng/kg/min; maintenance 2-10ng/kg/min, titrated by clinical response. Dilution: 3mcg/kg in 50mL NS/D5%, 1mL/hr = 1ng/kg/min. Apnoea/hypotension may occur at higher doses.
Incompatibilities: Levofloxacin, lipid
Storage after reconstitution: Fridge 14 days (pure); after dilution 24 hours, change infusion syringe every 24h
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Leaflet, KEMH, NeoFax, ANMF

name: Amikacin 250mg/2ml injection
Dose: Neonates (by PMA = GA + PNA): PMA <30 weeks 15mg/kg STAT, then 7.5mg/kg 24 hourly. PMA 30-<35 weeks 15mg/kg STAT, then 10mg/kg 24 hourly. PMA ≥35 weeks to term <7 days of life 15mg/kg 24 hourly. Term ≥7 days of life 25mg/kg STAT, then 18mg/kg 24 hourly. Infants & children 1 month-10 years: 25mg/kg STAT, then 18mg/kg 24 hourly [Max 22.5mg/kg/day or 1.5g/day]. Maintenance starts 24h after loading. TDM required. Use adjusted body weight if obese (correction factor 0.4).
Incompatibilities: Lipid, Amphothericin B, Ampicillin, Azithromycin, Diazepam, Ganciclovir, Heparin >1u/ml, Insulin, Imipenem/Cilastatin, Phenytoin, Propofol, Trimethoprim/Sulfamethoxazole, Thiopental
Method of administration: IV infusion over 1 hour; TDM 2nd dose post2 & post6 levels if OD dosing
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Leaflet, ANMF

name: Aminophyline 250mg/10ml injection
Dose: Apnea of prematurity: Loading 5mg/kg over 1h, maintenance 2-6mg/kg/day q12h starting 12h after loading. Acute severe bronchospasm: loading 10mg/kg over 1h, maintenance by age.
Incompatibilities: Amiodarone, Cefepime, Ceftriaxone, Cefotaxime, Ciprofloxacin, Clindamycin, Dobutamine, Epinephrine, Hydralazine, Insulin, Methylprednisolone, Morphine, C-penicillin, Phenytoin, Vancomycin
Ref: Leaflet, UpToDate, NeoFax, RCH

name: Amiodarone 150mg/3ml injection
Dose: SVT/JET Loading: 15mg/kg in 50ml D5% at 5ml/hr (25mcg/kg/min) for 4h, then maintenance 1-3ml/hr (5-15mcg/kg/min, max 1.2g/day). Pulseless VF/VT (CPR): 5mg/kg (max 300mg) rapid bolus, repeat twice to max 15mg/kg. VF/VT: Loading 5mg/kg over 1h, maintenance 5-25mcg/kg/min.
Incompatibilities: Aminophylline, Ampicillin, Ceftazidime, Cefazolin, Digoxin, Heparin, Imipenem-Cilastatin, Micafungin, Tazocin, Sodium bicarbonate, PN, lipid
Ref: NeoFax, ANMF, Uptodate

name: Amoxicillin & Clavulanic acid 1.2g injection (Augmentin)
Dose: ≤1 week of life: 30-60mg/kg/dose 12 hourly. >1 week: 30-60mg/kg/dose 8 hourly [Max 1.2g 8 hourly]. Dose based on combination of amoxicillin + clavulanic acid (5:1).
Incompatibilities: Glucose 5%/10%, sodium bicarbonate, PN, lipid emulsion, blood products, amiodarone, amikacin, ciprofloxacin, gentamicin, hydrocortisone, methylprednisolone, midazolam, metronidazole
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Starship, Leeds Teaching Hospital

name: Amoxicillin + Clavulanate 228mg/5ml syrup (Augmentin)
Dose: <35kg: 25-30mg/kg/dose BD [Max 625mg/dose]. Severe infection: 25-30mg/kg/dose TDS. Syrup is dosed on the AMOXICILLIN component only (7:1).
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026

name: Amoxicillin trihydrate 125mg/5ml syrup
Dose: <30kg: 25-30mg/kg/dose BD [Max 500mg/dose]. Infective endocarditis chemoprophylaxis: 50mg/kg single dose 30-60 min before procedure. Other (not in MGH guide): UTI prophylaxis 10-15mg/kg OD; asplenia 20mg/kg OD.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Product leaflet, ANMF

name: Amphothericin B 50mg (conventional) injection
Dose: 0.5mg/kg on Day 1, then 1mg/kg 24 hourly from Day 2 onwards [Max 1.5mg/kg/day]. Continuous infusion over 6 hours. Pre-medication required. Dilute with D5% only.
Incompatibilities: Single line, do not mix with other medications
Method of administration: IV infusion over 6 hours, single line; rapid infusion can cause CVS collapse
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Leaflet, Neomed

name: Ampicillin 1g & Sulbactam 0.5g injection (Unasyn)
Dose: Neonates ≤7 days of life: 75mg/kg/dose 12 hourly. Neonates ≥8 days, infants & children: 75mg/kg/dose 6 hourly. MDR Acinetobacter baumannii: <1 month 75mg/kg/dose 6 hourly; ≥1 month 150mg/kg/dose 6 hourly. Surgical prophylaxis: 75mg/kg [Max 3g]. Dose based on ampicillin + sulbactam (2:1).
Incompatibilities: Amiodarone, Ciprofloxacin
Method of administration: IV infusion over 30 mins; 3 hours for severe/MDR infections
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: IDSA 2014, Gkentzi 2020

name: Ampicillin 500mg injection
Dose: Neonates ≤7 days of life: 50mg/kg/dose 12 hourly. Neonates >7 days, infants & children: 50mg/kg/dose 6 hourly [Max 2g 6 hourly]. Meningitis (empirical/GBS): PNA ≤7 days 100mg/kg/dose 8 hourly; PNA >7 days 75mg/kg/dose 6 hourly. Infective endocarditis: 50mg/kg/dose 4-6 hourly [Max 12g/day].
Incompatibilities: Amikacin, Amiodarone, Dobutamine, Dopamine, Adrenaline, Erythromycin lactobionate, Fluconazole, Gentamicin, Hydralazine, Metoclopramide, Midazolam, Nicardipine, PN, Lipid, Sodium bicarbonate
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Neofax, leaflet, ANMF, Queensland Clinical Guideline

name: Arginine 5g/sachet
Dose: Oral: 250-500mg/kg/day in divided doses (depends on type of urea cycle defect - consult metabolic/genetic specialist). Dilute 1 sachet (5g) in 20ml cooled boiled water and serve with feeds. Stable 5 days in fridge.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Pharm-D info, Uptodate

name: Atropine 1mg/ml injection
Dose: Bradycardia: IV 0.01-0.02mg/kg over 1 min, repeat q10-15min, max 0.5mg/dose. ET: 0.04-0.06mg/kg. Intubation: IV/IM 0.01mg/kg. Preanaesthetic: PO 0.02mg/kg 1h before induction.
Incompatibilities: Adrenaline, Ampicillin, Heparin, Sodium bicarbonate, Thiopentone
Ref: RCH Melbourne, NeoFax, ANMF

name: Azithromycin 200mg/5ml granules (oral)
Dose: Atypical infection: 15mg/kg STAT [Max 500mg] Day 1, then 7.5mg/kg OD Day 2-5, OR 15mg/kg OD for 3 days. Pertussis <6 months: 10mg/kg/dose OD for 5 days. Ophthalmia neonatorum (Chlamydia): 20mg/kg/dose OD for 3 days. Avoid in neonates unless indicated (risk of IHPS).
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026

name: Azithromycin 500mg injection
Dose: 15mg/kg STAT [Max 500mg] on Day 1, then 5mg/kg 24 hourly [Max 250mg] Day 2-5. Pertussis: <6 months 10mg/kg/dose OD for 5 days. Avoid in neonates unless indicated (risk of infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis). Other (not in MGH guide): Ureaplasma eradication in preterm 20mg/kg OD IV x3 days.
Incompatibilities: Amikacin, Cefotaxime, Ceftazidime, Ceftriaxone, Cefuroxime, Clindamycin, Fentanyl, Frusemide, Gentamicin, Imipenem-Cilastatin, Morphine, Piperacillin-Tazobactam, Potassium chloride
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: KEMH & Perth Children's Hospital, ANMF

name: BCG vaccine freeze-dried injection
Dose: <12 months: 0.05mL intradermal (single dose at birth per NIP). >12 months: 0.1mL. Live-attenuated. No interval needed with immunoglobulins/blood products.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026

name: Benzathine Penicillin G 2.4 MIU injection
Dose: Congenital syphilis (defaulting risk): IM 50,000 u/kg single dose.
Ref: Paeds Protocol, NeoFax

name: Beractant intratracheal suspension 8ml
Dose: Intratracheal 4ml/kg/dose, max 8ml
Ref: Leaflet, NeoFax

name: C-penicillin/ Penicillin G/ Benzylpenicillin 1 MU injection
Dose: Neonates ≤7 days of life: 50,000-100,000 IU/kg/dose 12 hourly. Neonates >7 days, infants & children: 50,000-100,000 IU/kg/dose 6 hourly. Congenital syphilis: ≤7 days 50,000 IU/kg/dose 12 hourly; >7 days 50,000 IU/kg/dose 8 hourly (10 days if CSF normal, 14 days if abnormal; restart whole course if >1 day missed). Meningitis/GBS meningitis: PNA ≤7 days 150,000 IU/kg/dose 8 hourly; PNA 8-28 days 150,000 IU/kg/dose 6 hourly; infants 100,000 IU/kg/dose 6 hourly [Max 24 MU/day]. Infective endocarditis: 50,000 IU/kg/dose 4-6 hourly. 1mg = 1,667 IU.
Incompatibilities: Aminophylline, Amphoterin B, Dobutamine, Erythromycin, Ganciclovir, Heparin, Metoclopramide, Netilmicin, Noradrenaline, Phenobarbitone, Phenytoin, Potassium chloride, Protamine sulphate, Thiopentone, Tranexamic acid
Method of administration: IV infusion over 30 minutes; separate from aminoglycoside with a flush (penicillins inactivate aminoglycosides)
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Leaflet, NeoFax

name: Caffeine citrate 20mg/ml injection
Dose: Apnoea of prematurity (IV/oral) - doses as caffeine CITRATE: loading 20mg/kg; maintenance 5-10mg/kg OD. Dose may be optimised by clinical response, or kept static to allow self-weaning as weight increases. Unit tiered maintenance (citrate): week 1 5mg/kg, week 2 6mg/kg, week 3-4 7mg/kg, week 5-8 8mg/kg OD. Switch to oral once feeds ≥100ml/kg/day.
Incompatibilities: Aciclovir, adenosine, furosemide, pantoprazole
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Leaflet, NeoFax, UpToDate, Canterbury DHB, KEMH, ANMF 2022

name: Caffeine citrate 20mg/ml oral solution
Dose: Apnoea of prematurity - doses as caffeine CITRATE: loading 20mg/kg; maintenance 5-10mg/kg OD (unit tiers: week 1 5, week 2 6, week 3-4 7, week 5-8 8mg/kg). May oralise once feeds ≥100ml/kg/day.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: ANMF

name: Calcitriol 0.25mcg/mL oral liquid (extemporaneous)
Dose: 0.02mcg/kg OD, adjust to response (usual 0.25-0.5mcg/day). Active vitamin D3 (does not need liver/kidney activation).
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026

name: Calcium carbonate 500mg tablet (oral)
Dose: Ward practice: neonates 125mg (50mg elemental calcium) QID; 1 month-3 years 250mg (100mg elemental) BD-QID. Dose range 20-100mg/kg/day elemental calcium in divided doses, titrated to calcium level. 1 tablet (500mg) = 200mg elemental calcium. Prescribe as whole-tablet fraction (round to nearest quarter/half).
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Freshly prepare; solution will be cloudy, tablet may not fully dissolve. Avoid combining with phosphate/iron/EBM+HMF in the same dose.
Method of administration: Separate from phosphate, iron, thyroxine, phenytoin by ≥2 hours; serve with feeding, not mixed into milk syringe
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: KEMH & Perth Children's Hospital, SGH formulary

name: Calcium gluconate 10% (1g/10ml) injection
Dose: Fast correction: 0.5mL/kg (50mg/kg) over 30-60 minutes [Max 20mL/dose]. Continuous infusion for symptomatic hypocalcaemia: 8-32mg/kg/hour. Dilute: peripheral 1:5 with NS/dextrose (max 0.04mmol/mL); central 1:1 (max 0.1mmol/mL). 1mL = 0.23mmol Ca = 9.3mg elemental Ca. Cardiac monitoring; extravasation causes necrosis - monitor site.
Incompatibilities: PN, lipids, Amphotericin, Ceftriaxone, Clindamycin, Dobutamine, Digoxin, Fluconazole, Phosphate, Sodium Bicarbonate
Method of administration: IV bolus slowly over 60 min, not exceeding 100mg/min; via central line whenever possible
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: NeoFax, UpToDate

name: Calcium lactate 300mg tablet
Dose: Dose range 20-100mg/kg/day elemental calcium in divided doses, titrated to calcium level. 1 tablet (300mg) = 39mg elemental calcium. Prescribe as whole-tablet fraction.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026

name: Calcium Polystyrene Sulphonate Powder (Kalimate)
Dose: Hyperkalaemia: 0.3-0.6g/kg [Max 30g/dose] 6 hourly. NEONATES: RECTAL ONLY (reduced gut motility). Rectal prep: dilute 5g (1 sachet) in 20ml NS (0.25g/ml), shake, draw dose (may dilute further with water); irrigate colon 8-12h later with 1-2ml NS at a time to remove resin.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: ANMF, SESLHD

name: Captopril 1mg/mL syrup (extemporaneous)
Dose: Anti-failure - neonates: 0.05-0.1mg/kg/dose TDS, gradually increase up to 0.3mg/kg/dose TDS. Anti-hypertensive - neonates: 0.01-0.1mg/kg/dose TDS, may titrate up to 0.5mg/kg/dose TDS [Max 2mg/kg/day]. Infants/children: 0.1mg/kg/dose TDS, adjust to response.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026

name: Cefazolin Sodium 1g Injection
Dose: 10-15mg/kg/dose 8 hourly. Severe infection: 50mg/kg/dose 6 hourly OR 50mg/kg STAT then 200mg/kg/day in 6 divided doses [Max 2g 6 hourly]. Surgical prophylaxis: 30-50mg/kg [Max 2g].
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: NAG 2024

name: Cefepime 1g injection
Dose: Neonates: 50mg/kg/dose 12 hourly. Infants & children: 50mg/kg/dose 8 hourly [Max 2g 8 hourly].
Incompatibilities: Acyclovir, Aminophylline, Amphotericin B, Diazepam, Dobutamine, Dopamine, Erythromycin lactobionate, Ganciclovir, Magnesium sulphate, Metoclopramide, Midazolam, Morphine, Nicardipine, Phenytoin, Vancomycin
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Leaflet, Neofax, NAG 2024

name: Cefotaxime 1g injection
Dose: Neonates ≤7 days of life: 50mg/kg/dose 12 hourly. >7-28 days: 50mg/kg/dose 8 hourly. Infants & children: 50mg/kg/dose 6 hourly [Max 2g 6 hourly]. Meningitis: ≤7 days 50mg/kg/dose 8 hourly; >7 days, infants & children 50mg/kg/dose 6 hourly. Ophthalmia neonatorum: IV/IM 100mg/kg single dose. Surgical prophylaxis: 50mg/kg [Max 2g].
Incompatibilities: Azithromycin, Fluconazole, Protamine sulphate, Sodium bicarbonate, Vancomycin
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Leaflet, ANMF, UpToDate, NAG 2024

name: Ceftazidime 1g injection
Dose: Neonates ≤7 days of life: 50mg/kg/dose 12 hourly. >7-28 days: 50mg/kg/dose 8 hourly. Infants & children: 50mg/kg/dose 6-8 hourly. Melioidosis: 50mg/kg/dose 6 hourly, infuse over 3 hours [Max 2g 6 hourly].
Incompatibilities: Amiodarone, Azithromycin, Erythromycin lactobionate, Fluconazole, Midazolam, Phenytoin, Nicardipine, Vancomycin
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Leaflet, ANMF, NeoFax

name: Ceftriaxone 1g injection
Dose: AVOID IN NEONATES (risk of kernicterus). Infants & children: general 50-100mg/kg/day in 1-2 divided doses. Meningitis/severe infection: 50mg/kg/dose 12 hourly. Salmonella (no CNS involvement): 80-100mg/kg/day 24 hourly. Surgical prophylaxis: 50-75mg/kg [Max 2g].
Incompatibilities: Aminophylline, Azithromycin, Calcium gluconate, Fluconazole, Vancomycin
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: UpToDate, Micromedex

name: Cefuroxime 750mg injection
Dose: Neonates ≤7 days of life: 50mg/kg/dose 12 hourly. Neonates >8 days: 50mg/kg/dose 8 hourly. Infants & children: 25-50mg/kg/dose 8 hourly [Max 1.5g 8 hourly].
Incompatibilities: Clarithromycin, fluconazole, gentamicin, midazolam, sodium bicarbonate, vancomycin
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Leeds Teaching Hospital

name: Cephalexin monohydrate 125mg/5ml syrup
Dose: 12.5mg/kg/dose QID [Max 500mg] OR 25mg/kg/dose BD [Max 1g]. Severe infection: 25mg/kg/dose QID. UTI prophylaxis: 12.5mg/kg/dose ON.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026

name: Chloral hydrate mixture 100mg/mL
Dose: Oral sedation: 10-50mg/kg/dose TDS/QID, not exceeding 200mg/kg/day [Max 1g/dose; may repeat up to cumulative 2g on a single occasion]. Give at least 30 min before procedure. Onset 15-30 min, duration 1-2 h. No analgesic effect.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026

name: Cholecalciferol (Vitamin D3) 1000iu capsule
Dose: Vitamin D deficiency treatment: usual starting dose 1000 IU OD, reassess and titrate - <3 months 2000 IU OD; 3-12 months 2000 IU OD. Minimum duration 90 days. Quota drug - submit application for new patients.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Freshly prepare
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Global Consensus on Nutritional Rickets 2016, NeoFax, SGH formulary

name: Cloxacillin 500mg injection
Dose: Neonates ≤7 days of life: 50mg/kg/dose 12 hourly. >7-28 days: 50mg/kg/dose 8 hourly. Infants & children: 25-50mg/kg/dose 6 hourly. Severe infection: 50mg/kg/dose 4 hourly, or continuous infusion 300mg/kg/day [Max 2g 4 hourly or 12g/day].
Incompatibilities: Gentamicin, lipids, pantoprazole, morphine
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Leaflet, UpToDate

name: Colistin (Polymyxin E) 1 MIU injection
Dose: Neb for MDR Acinetobacter VAP: colistin base 4mg/kg 12h up to 14 days. IV: Load 200,000 unit/kg over 30 min, then 200,000 unit/kg/day in 3 divided doses.
Ref: Leaflet, UpToDate, KEMH, NeoFax

name: Dexamethasone 8mg/2ml injection
Dose: Post-extubation stridor: neonates IV 0.25mg/kg/dose TDS for a total of 3 doses (longer in severe cases); infants & children IV 0.25mg/kg/dose QID. Low-dose DART (oral, 12 hourly): Day 1-3 0.075mg/kg/dose; Day 4-6 0.05mg/kg/dose; Day 7-8 0.025mg/kg/dose; Day 9-10 0.01mg/kg/dose, then off. Croup: mild 0.15mg/kg single dose (may repeat at 12 and 24h); moderate 0.3-0.6mg/kg; severe IV 0.6mg/kg. Other (not in MGH guide): moderate-dose regimen for term CLD (ANMF 2022) 0.25mg/kg 12h x3d, 0.15 x3d, 0.1 x3d, 0.05 x3d, 0.025 x6d then off.
Incompatibilities: Glycopyrrolate, Midazolam, Vancomycin
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Leaflet, KEMH, Neomed, Paed Protocol 4th ed

name: Dexmedetomidine HCl 100mcg/mL Injection
Dose: CONTRAINDICATED in heart block/severe ventricular dysfunction. <37w GA: loading 0.2mcg/kg over 15min (if needed), maintenance 0.2mcg/kg/hr, max 1mcg/kg/hr. Term <=14d: loading 0.35mcg/kg, maintenance 0.3mcg/kg/hr, max 1.2mcg/kg/hr. Term >14d: loading 0.5mcg/kg, maintenance 0.5-0.75mcg/kg/hr, max 1.5mcg/kg/hr. NOT FOR IV RESCUE BOLUS.
Incompatibilities: Amphotericin B forms, diazepam, ketamine, pantoprazole, phenytoin

name: Diazepam 10mg/2ml injection / 5mg/2.5ml rectal solution
Dose: IV: 0.2mg/kg/dose [Max 10mg]. Rectal: 0.3-0.5mg/kg [Max 5mg/dose]; if still fitting may repeat once (cumulative max 10mg); round to nearest 2.5mg. Oral: 0.04-0.2mg/kg/dose BD-QID. WARNING: IV diazepam brand Zopam contains benzyl alcohol - NOT for use in <2 years old.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026

name: Digoxin 500mcg/2ml injection
Dose: Consult paediatric cardiologist before initiating. Loading: 15mcg/kg stat, then 5mcg/kg after 6h, then maintenance 3-5mcg/kg q12h (max 200mcg IV/250mcg oral). Reduce dose ~20-25% when switching oral→IV. Renal impairment: reduce dose by ≥50%.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Dilute to at least 4-fold volume with diluent to avoid precipitation; max concentration 62.5mcg/mL
Incompatibilities: Adrenaline, Amiodarone, Caspofungin, Dobutamine, Fluconazole, Propofol
Method of administration: IV over 30-60 minutes; TDM level 12-24h after loading dose (pre-dose level)
Ref: NeoFax, ANMF

name: Dobutamine 250mg/20ml injection
Dose: Peripheral line: 15mg/kg in 50ml NS/D5% (1ml/hr = 5mcg/kg/min, max 4ml/hr = 20mcg/kg/min). Central line: 30mg/kg in 50ml (1ml/hr = 10mcg/kg/min, max 2ml/hr = 20mcg/kg/min).
Incompatibilities: Acyclovir, Aminophylline, Cefepime, Bumetanide, Diazepam, Digoxin, Frusemide, Micafungin, Phenytoin, Tazocin, Sodium bicarbonate
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Leaflet, NeoFax, ANMF

name: Domperidone 1mg/ml suspension
Dose: Oral 0.2-0.5mg/kg/dose TDS-QID (up to 4 hourly in severe reflux symptoms) [Max 10mg/dose]. Give 30 minutes before feeding.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026

name: Dopamine 200mg/5ml injection
Dose: Peripheral line: 15mg/kg in 50ml NS/D5% (1ml/hr = 5mcg/kg/min, max 4ml/hr = 20mcg/kg/min). Central line: 30mg/kg in 50ml (1ml/hr = 10mcg/kg/min, max 2ml/hr = 20mcg/kg/min).
Incompatibilities: Acyclovir, Amphotericin B, Ampicillin, Cefepime, Frusemide, Insulin, Penicillin G, Sodium bicarbonate
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Leaflet, NeoFax

name: Enalapril maleate 1mg/mL suspension (extemporaneous)
Dose: Anti-hypertensive, ≥1 month old: initial 0.1mg/kg/day OD-BD [Max 5mg/day], adjust to BP response up to 0.6mg/kg/day [Max 40mg/day].
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026

name: Enoxaparin 20mg/0.2ml injection
Dose: Prophylaxis: SC 0.75 mg/kg/dose q12h. Treatment: preterm 1.5-2 mg/kg/dose q12h; term 1.5-1.7 mg/kg/dose q12h. Adjust to anti-Xa level (target range per local lab). Duration typically 6 weeks-3 months depending on thrombus site/response.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Dilute pre-filled syringe with NS to 20mg/1mL (1mg/0.05mL) for accurate small-volume dosing
Ref: NeoFax 2020, UpToDate

name: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate 200mg/5ml suspension
Dose: Antibacterial: 20-25mg/kg/dose BD [Max 800mg BD]. Prokinetic: 2mg/kg/dose TDS (high dose 12.5mg/kg/dose TDS short-term e.g. 10 days for specific cases) [Max 250mg TDS]. Caution <6 months - risk of infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026

name: Erythropoietin (Epoetin alfa) injection
Dose: Anaemia of prematurity (only if unit protocol uses EPO): 200-250 units/kg SC/IV, 3 times weekly. Ensure adequate iron supplementation concurrently. Confirm local protocol/indication before starting — not all units use routine EPO.
Ref: NeoFax 2020 — unit-dependent, confirm local practice

name: Fentanyl citrate 0.1mg/2ml injection
Dose: IV bolus (sedation/analgesia): 1mcg/kg/dose [Max 100mcg]. Infusion ≤10kg: 100mcg/kg in 50ml NS/D5% (1ml/hr = 2mcg/kg/hr, max 2ml/hr = 4mcg/kg/hr). Ventilated patient: up to 5mcg/kg/hr, max 10mcg/kg/hr. Pre-medication for intubation (unit RSI): 2mcg/kg slowly over ≥5 min. Reversal: naloxone.
Incompatibilities: Azithromycin, Pantoprazole, Phenytoin, Thiopentone, Bactrim
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: NeoFax, NeoMed, leaflet, ANMF

name: Fluconazole 100mg capsule (oral)
Dose: Treatment: 25mg/kg STAT Day 1, then 12mg/kg OD. Superficial infection: 6mg/kg STAT Day 1, then 3mg/kg OD. Prophylaxis after treated Candida sepsis with ongoing risk: 6mg/kg/dose twice weekly.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026

name: Fluconazole 100mg/50ml injection
Dose: Treatment: 25mg/kg STAT, then 12mg/kg 24 hourly. Prophylaxis in infants after completing treatment for Candida sepsis but still at risk of recurrence: 6mg/kg/dose twice per week. Superficial infection: 6mg/kg STAT Day 1, then 3mg/kg 24 hourly from Day 2.
Incompatibilities: Ampicillin, calcium gluconate, cefotaxime, ceftazidime, ceftriaxone, clindamycin, digoxin, frusemide, imipenem-cilastatin, pentamidine
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Neomed, leaflet, Perth Children Hospital

name: Flumazenil 0.5mg/5ml injection
Dose: Benzodiazepine reversal: IV 0.005mg/kg/dose [Max 0.2mg/dose], repeat every 1 minute until fully reversed; cumulative max 0.05mg/kg or 1mg, whichever is smaller.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026

name: Folic acid 1mg/ml oral solution
Dose: Neonate: 0.2mg OD. Infant: 0.5-1mg OD. 1mg = 1mL.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Compounded; shake well before use
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: ANMF, SGH formulary

name: Frusemide (Furosemide) 10mg/ml oral solution
Dose: Anti-failure/fluid overload: PO 0.5-1mg/kg/dose OD-QID.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: NeoFax, SGH formulary

name: Frusemide (Furosemide) 20mg/2ml injection
Dose: Anti-failure/fluid overload: IV slow bolus 0.5-1mg/kg/dose OD-QID. IV infusion (severe overload): 0.1-1mg/kg/hour. Infusion dilution ≤20kg: 10mg/kg in 20mL NS, 1mL/hr = 0.5mg/kg/hr.
Incompatibilities: Azithromycin, Caffeine, Caspofungin, Ciprofloxacin, Dobutamine, Dopamine, Fluconazole, Gentamicin, Hydralazine, Metoclopramide, Midazolam, Milrinone, Netilmicin, Nicardipine, Vancomycin, Vasopressin
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: NeoFax, SGH formulary

name: Ganciclovir sodium 500mg/10ml injection
Dose: Symptomatic congenital CMV infection: 6 mg/kg/dose IV q12h for minimum 6 weeks, then transition to oral valganciclovir to complete 6 months total treatment where possible. CYTOTOXIC drug.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Prepared by cytotoxic drug reconstitution service only
Incompatibilities: Lipid, Cefepime, Piperacillin/Tazobactam
Method of administration: IV infusion over 1 hour, flush before/after with NS
Ref: NeoFax, SGH formulary

name: Gentamicin 80mg/2ml injection
Dose: By PMA (GA + PNA): PMA ≤29 weeks: ≤7 days of life 5mg/kg 48 hourly; 8-28 days 4mg/kg 36 hourly; ≥29 days 4mg/kg 24 hourly. PMA 30-34 weeks: ≤7 days 4.5mg/kg 36 hourly; ≥8 days 4mg/kg 24 hourly. PMA ≥35 weeks (<1 month old): 4mg/kg 24 hourly. Infants ≥1 month-10 years: 5mg/kg/dose 24 hourly. Infective endocarditis (synergy): 1mg/kg/dose 8 hourly. TDM required. Use adjusted body weight if obese (correction factor 0.4).
Incompatibilities: Amphotericin B, Ampicillin, Azithromycin, Frusemide, Imipenem/Cilastatin, Heparin >1u/ml, Indomethacin, Propofol
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Leaflet, Neofax

name: Glucagon 1mg/ml injection
Dose: Persistent hypoglycemia: 0.5-1mg stat IV/IM/SC, then IVI 5-10mcg/kg/hr (dilution 0.25mg/kg in 25ml D10%, 1ml/hr=10mcg/kg/hr).
Incompatibilities: Solutions containing calcium
Ref: ANMF, Paeds Protocol

name: Glycerin 25% & Sodium chloride 15% enema 20ml (Ravin)
Dose: Neonates: 0.3-0.5ml/dose (NOT per kg). Infants & children: 0.5ml/kg (may round to nearest 5ml).
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026

name: Glycopyrrolate 200mcg/ml injection
Dose: Reduction of respiratory secretions/drooling: IV/SC 4mcg/kg/dose TDS-QID, may increase to 10mcg/kg/dose TDS-QID. Oral (100mcg/ml syrup, extemporaneous): 20-100mcg/kg/dose TDS [Max 3mg/dose].
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026

name: Heparin 25,000 IU/5ml injection
Dose: Maintaining CVL patency: 0.5-1ml/hr. Thrombosis/PE treatment: loading 75unit/kg over 10min, then 20-30 unit/kg/hr, adjust by APTT. Heparin lock: 10 units/mL, 0.5-1mL per lumen.
Incompatibilities: Amikacin, Amiodarone, Caspofungin, Diazepam, Gentamicin, Netilmicin, Phenytoin, Vancomycin

name: Hepatitis B immunoglobulin 100 IU/0.5mL injection
Dose: Hepatitis B post-exposure prophylaxis in neonates (regardless of weight and age): 100 IU IM STAT.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026

name: Hepatitis B vaccine 10mcg (paediatric)
Dose: 0.5mL (10mcg) IM at birth per NIP. If birth dose deferred because BW <1.8kg, give at 1 month of age or at hospital discharge, whichever is earlier.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026

name: Human Albumin 20% injection
Dose: Hypoalbuminaemia/oedema: 20% albumin 0.5-1g/kg (2.5-5ml/kg) over 2-4 hours. Hypovolaemia (plasma expansion): 5% albumin 0.5-1g/kg (10-20ml/kg) over 2-4 hours - volume of 20% needed = (5% x volume of 5% ordered) / 20%. Do NOT dilute with WFI (fatal haemolysis).
Diluent: NS, D5, D10, 0.45% NaCl, D5NS. DO NOT dilute with WFI (haemolysis risk)
Incompatibilities: TPN, Lipid, Micafungin, Midazolam, Vancomycin, Verapamil
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Leaflet, NeoFax

name: Human immunoglobulin (IVIG) 5g/50ml (10%) injection
Dose: Immune haemolytic disease: 0.5-1g/kg over 2 hours, may repeat in 12 hours. ITP: 0.8g/kg single dose (severe bleed 1g/kg); one repeat at 24-48h if inadequate, total ≤2g/kg. Chickenpox post-exposure prophylaxis: 0.4g/kg within 96 hours. Follow Hospital Miri IVIG Infusion Protocol; digital IVIG request form approved by authorised specialist. Round up to nearest bottle.
Incompatibilities: Single line, do not mix with other medications
Method of administration: IV infusion, typically over 10 hours — follow unit IVIG infusion protocol
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: UpToDate, SGH formulary

name: Hydrochlorothiazide 25mg tablet
Dose: Anti-failure: neonates 1-1.5mg/kg/dose OD-BD [Max 4mg/kg/day]; infants <2 years 1-1.5mg/kg/dose OD-BD [Max 37.5mg/day]. Also used with diazoxide for hypoglycaemia (offsets fluid retention).
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Compounded to 5mg/mL; give morning dose as early as possible
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: SGH extemp formulary

name: Hydrocortisone sodium succinate 100mg injection
Dose: Acute asthma (MGH): 4mg/kg/dose QID [Max 100mg/dose]. Other (not in MGH guide): persistent hypoglycaemia 1-2mg/kg 8-12 hourly; early neonatal hypotension 2mg/kg stat then 1mg/kg 8-12 hourly; CAH 10-15mg/m2/day in 3 doses.
Incompatibilities: Frusemide, Midazolam, Phenobarbital, Phenytoin
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Leaflet, NeoFax

name: Ibuprofen 100mg/5mL oral suspension
Dose: PDA closure, high-dose therapy (≥72 hours of life): 3 doses at 24-hour intervals - Day 1 20mg/kg, Day 2 & 3 10mg/kg. Analgesia/antipyretic: 3-6 months 5mg/kg/dose TDS; ≥6 months 5-10mg/kg/dose TDS.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026

name: Ibuprofen 10mg/2ml injection (Pedea)
Dose: PDA closure, MGH high-dose therapy (≥72 hours of life): 3 doses at 24-hour intervals - Day 1 20mg/kg, Day 2 & 3 10mg/kg. Standard dose (alternative, e.g. <72h of life): 10mg/kg, then 5mg/kg at 24h and 48h. See PDA tab for weight-calculated doses.
Incompatibilities: Do not mix with other drugs in same line
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: NeoFax 2020, PP5

name: Imipenem & Cilastatin 500mg/500mg injection
Dose: Dose based on imipenem component: 1st week 25mg/kg 12h. After 1st week 25mg/kg 8h.
Incompatibilities: Amikacin, Amiodarone, Azithromycin, Fluconazole, Gentamicin, Lorazepam, Milrinone, Sodium bicarbonate
Ref: Leaflet, UpToDate

name: Indometacin (Indomethacin) 1mg injection
Dose: PDA closure, age-based 3-dose course: <48h 0.2/0.1/0.1 mg/kg; 2-7 days 0.2/0.2/0.2 mg/kg; >7 days 0.2/0.25/0.25 mg/kg, given 12-24 hourly (24h as local default). Withhold subsequent dose if urine output <0.6mL/kg/h until renal function recovers. See PDA tab for weight-calculated doses.
Diluent: Preservative-free NS or WFI per product; do not further dilute after reconstitution per manufacturer
Incompatibilities: Do not mix with other drugs in same line
Ref: NeoFax 2020, PP5

name: Iron Polymaltose complex [10mg elemental iron/mL]
Dose: NICU/SCN practice: prophylaxis 0.3mL/kg OD (3mg/kg/day); treatment 0.3mL/kg BD (6mg/kg/day). General: prophylaxis 2mg/kg elemental iron OD; treatment 6mg/kg OD. 1mL = 10mg elemental iron.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: SGH formulary

name: Ketamine 10mg/ml injection
Dose: IV bolus sedation: 1mg/kg/dose, up to 2mg/kg/dose. Onset 1-2 min, duration 15-60 min.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026

name: L-arginine 5g/10ml injection
Dose: Urea cycle defect/hyperammonaemia, body weight ≤20kg: loading 250mg/kg over 90-120 minutes, then maintenance 250mg/kg/day over 24 hours. Mix with sodium benzoate and sodium phenylbutyrate (each 250mg/kg) together in D10% to a total of 50ml (max concentration 50mg/ml - for doses ≥2500mg increase the final volume). Maintenance: same dose and dilution over 24 hours. Avoid in arginase deficiency.
Incompatibilities: Single line, only mixable with sodium benzoate & sodium phenylbutyrate
Method of administration: IV infusion via large vein/central line
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: NeoFax

name: Lactulose 3.35g/5mL liquid
Dose: Constipation: 0.5ml/kg/dose OD-TDS [Max 60ml/day]; may increase to QID according to stool consistency.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026

name: Levetiracetam 500mg/5ml injection
Dose: Status epilepticus: IV loading 40mg/kg over 10-15 minutes, then 20-30mg/kg/dose BD. Epilepsy (IV/oral): 7mg/kg/dose BD, may increase to 60mg/kg/day [Max 3g/day]; higher doses may be used in refractory cases.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Leaflet, NeoFax, Leeds Teaching Hospital, Paed protocol, ANMF

name: Levothyroxine (L-thyroxine) 25mcg & 50mcg tablet
Dose: Congenital hypothyroidism, by FT4 severity: subclinical 5-10mcg/kg/dose OD; mild (FT4>10) 10mcg/kg/dose OD; moderate (FT4 5-10) 10mcg/kg/dose OD; severe (FT4<5) 15mcg/kg/dose OD.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Freshly prepare each dose; note two strengths available (25 & 50mcg) — check carefully
Ref: Consensus Guidelines on Congenital Hypothyroidism Malaysia, UpToDate

name: Lidocaine 25mg & Prilocaine 25mg cream (EMLA)
Dose: Topical local anaesthesia for procedures (PICC, LP, venepuncture): 0.5-1g applied 30-60 minutes before procedure. NOT recommended for preterm infants <37 weeks GA — risk of methaemoglobinaemia.
Method of administration: Apply topically under occlusive dressing, remove before procedure
Ref: Product leaflet, SGH formulary

name: Linezolid 2mg/ml injection
Dose: Selected resistant Gram-positive infections (e.g. MRSA not responding to vancomycin): 10 mg/kg/dose IV/PO TDS (infants and children <12 years).
Ref: UpToDate, NeoFax

name: Magnesium sulphate 2.465g/5ml injection
Dose: Hypomagnesaemia: 50mg/kg (0.1mL/kg) over 4 hours [Max 4mL (2g) per correction]; dilute 1:5 with NS/D5% (max 100mg/mL). PPHN: loading 50mg/kg over 30 minutes, maintenance 20-50mg/kg/hour, adjust by response. Acute asthma: loading 50mg/kg (0.1ml/kg) in 20ml NS over 20 min [Max 2g]; maintenance from 30mg/kg/hour (range 10-50mg/kg/hour). Usual maintenance dilution 2.5g in 25ml NS (100mg/ml). Keep serum Mg 1.5-2.5mmol/L.
Incompatibilities: Lipid, Amiodarone, Amphothericin B, Calcium chloride, Cefepime, Pantoprazole, Sodium bicarbonate
Method of administration: IV infusion over 4 hours, max rate 0.04mmol/kg/min
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Leaflet, Leeds Teaching Hospitals, ANMF

name: Magnesium sulphate 2.5g/5mL mixture (oral)
Dose: Maintenance: start 0.05g/kg (0.2mmol/kg) OD-QID, may increase to 0.2g/kg/dose (0.8mmol/kg/dose) [Max 2.5g/dose], titrate to Mg level and tolerance (diarrhoea). Prescribe in grams; volume (mL) = 2 x grams.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026

name: Meropenem 500mg injection
Dose: Neonates ≤7 days of life: 20-40mg/kg 12 hourly. Neonates >7 days, infants & children: 20-40mg/kg 8 hourly [Max 2g 8 hourly]. Antibiotic request form on initiation; review form if continued >72h. Other (not in MGH guide): severe infection 120mg/kg/day in 6 divided doses infused over 4h; renal adjustment by eGFR.
Incompatibilities: Acyclovir, Amphotericin B, calcium gluconate, Metronidazole, sodium bicarbonate, Zidovudine
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Leaflet, Neofax

name: Metronidazole 200mg/5ml suspension (oral)
Dose: Neonates (≤28 days): 15mg/kg STAT, then 7.5mg/kg 12 hourly (<2kg start maintenance after 48h; >2kg after 24h). Infants: 15mg/kg STAT, then 7.5mg/kg 8 hourly. C. difficile: 10mg/kg/dose TDS [Max 400mg TDS].
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026

name: Metronidazole 500mg/100ml injection
Dose: Neonates (≤28 days of life): 15mg/kg STAT, then 7.5mg/kg 12 hourly (<2kg start maintenance after 48h; >2kg after 24h). Infants & children: 15mg/kg STAT, then 7.5mg/kg 8 hourly, starting 8h after loading [Max 500mg 8 hourly].
Incompatibilities: Meropenem
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Leaflet, Neofax

name: Micafungin sodium 50mg injection
Dose: Invasive/systemic candidiasis: neonates & infants <4 months 10 mg/kg IV OD (up to 15mg/kg/day reported for extremely premature infants or resistant strains — confirm with ID/pharmacy); infants >4 months 4 mg/kg IV OD.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Reconstitute with 5mL NS to 50mg/5mL; dilute further to final concentration 0.5-1.5mg/mL (central line if 1.6-4mg/mL)
Incompatibilities: Albumin, Amiodarone, Dobutamine, Adrenaline, Insulin, Levofloxacin, Midazolam, Morphine, Phenytoin, Rocuronium
Method of administration: IV infusion over 1 hour, protect from light during infusion
Ref: NeoFax 2020, ANMF

name: Midazolam 5mg/1ml, 5mg/5ml injection
Dose: Status epilepticus: IV 0.2mg/kg bolus [Max 10mg]; infusion 3-5mcg/kg/min up to max 15mcg/kg/min. Sedation: IV bolus 0.1-0.5mg/kg/dose; infusion 1-4mcg/kg/min. Infusion dilution: 3mg/kg in 50ml NS/D5% (1ml/hr = 1mcg/kg/min). Reversal: flumazenil. Give boluses slowly over 2-5 min (hypotension/seizure risk).
Incompatibilities: Lipids, Acyclovir, Albumin, Aminophylline, Amoxicillin, Ampicillin, Azithromycin, Cefepime, Ceftazidime, Dexamethasone, Ertapenem, Esomeprazole, Cloxacillin, Frusemide, Ganciclovir, Hydrocortisone sodium succinate, Imipenem-cilastatin, Omeprazole, Phenobarbitone, Piperacillin-tazobactam, Sodium bicarbonate, Thiopentone, Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Leaflet, NeoFax, Paeds Protocol 4th Ed

name: Milrinone 10mg/10ml injection
Dose: NICU practice: loading (optional) 75mcg/kg over 1 hour - 1.5mg/kg in 50mL NS/D5%, run 2.5mL/hr for 1 hour. Maintenance 0.5-0.75mcg/kg/min - same dilution, 1mL/hr = 0.5mcg/kg/min. ANMF caution: loading risks hypotension, especially in preterm infants - often omitted.
Incompatibilities: Frusemide, Imipenem/Cilastatin, Procainamide
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: NeoFax, leaflet, UpToDate

name: Morphine 10mg/1ml injection
Dose: Neonates, infants & children: oral/IV 0.1mg/kg/dose QID, adjust to response (procedural sedation bolus 0.1-0.2mg/kg, max 10mg). Continuous infusion 10-40mcg/kg/hour. Dilution: 0.5mg/kg in 50ml NS/D5% (1ml/hr = 10mcg/kg/hr) OR 1mg/kg in 50ml (1ml/hr = 20mcg/kg/hr, max 4ml/hr = 80mcg/kg/hr). Reversal: naloxone.
Incompatibilities: Azithromycin, Cefepime, Micafungin, Phenobarbitone, Phenytoin
Method of administration: Slow bolus over 5 minutes or continuous infusion
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Leaflet, NeoFax

name: Multivitamin drops
Dose: ≤12 months: 1mL OD (Appeton Baby Drops). Per 1mL: vitamin A 1333 U, vitamin D3 438 U, vitamin E 6.57 U, B1 218mcg, B2 336mcg, B6 108mcg, nicotinamide 2.15mg.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Commercial product, shake well before use
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Product leaflet, SGH formulary

name: Naloxone HCl 0.4 mg/1ml injection
Dose: Opioid reversal: IV 0.01mg/kg/dose [Max 0.4mg/dose], repeat every 2 minutes until fully reversed [cumulative max 2mg]. CONTRAINDICATED during resuscitation/treatment of neonates born to known or suspected opioid-dependent mothers.
Incompatibilities: Sodium bicarbonate
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: ANMF, UpToDate

name: Netilmicin 150mg/1.5ml injection
Dose: BW<1200g: day0-7 5mg/kg 48h; day8-30 5mg/kg 36h; >30d 5mg/kg 24h. BW1200-2500g: day0-7 5mg/kg 36h; >7d 5mg/kg 24h. Term: day0-7 5mg/kg 24h; 1wk-10y 8mg/kg day1 then 6mg/kg 24h.
Incompatibilities: Ampicillin, Frusemide, Heparin >1u/ml, C-pen, Propofol
Ref: NeoFax, leaflet, ANMF

name: Noradrenaline 4mg/4ml injection
Dose: Peripheral line: 0.15mg/kg in 50ml D5% (preferred) or NS (1ml/hr = 0.05mcg/kg/min, max 40ml/hr = 2mcg/kg/min). Central line: 0.3mg/kg in 50ml (1ml/hr = 0.1mcg/kg/min, max 20ml/hr = 2mcg/kg/min).
Incompatibilities: Insulin, Aminophylline, Amphotericin B, Diazepam, Ganciclovir, Phenobarbital, Phenytoin, Sodium bicarbonate, Bactrim
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Leaflet, NeoFax

name: Nystatin 100,000 units/ml suspension
Dose: Prophylaxis of invasive candidiasis - neonates: 100,000 units TDS (dose NOT per kg). Prophylaxis of oral candidiasis - infants <1 year: 50,000 units TDS. Treatment of oral candidiasis - neonates & infants <1 year: 100,000 units QID. Coat around the oral cavity; do NOT give via NG tube (no systemic absorption). Unit practice: eligible <1500g with central lines/broad-spectrum antibiotics/prolonged steroids; stop BW<1000g at day 28, BW1000-1499g when lines out/antibiotics stopped/3 days after steroids.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: NeoFax, leaflet

name: Omeprazole 2mg/ml suspension (extemporaneous)
Dose: Oral 0.4-0.8mg/kg/dose OD-BD, 1 hour before feeding. IV (omeprazole 40mg injection): 1mg/kg/dose OD-BD. NG-fed patients: prescribe suspension (granules may block NG tube).
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026

name: Oseltamivir 60mg/5ml suspension (12mg/ml)
Dose: Infants <9 months: 3mg/kg/dose BD. 9-<12 months: 3.5mg/kg/dose BD. Best efficacy if started within 48 hours of symptom onset.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026

name: Palivizumab 100mg injection
Dose: RSV prophylaxis: 15mg/kg/dose IM once a month for a total of 5 doses.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026

name: Pantoprazole 40mg injection
Dose: Upper GI bleeding: ≤40kg 2mg/kg STAT, then 0.2mg/kg/hr (max duration 72 hours). Infusion dilution: 40mg in 40ml NS, run 0.2ml/kg/hr = 0.2mg/kg/hr. Other (not in MGH guide): IV 1mg/kg OD-BD.
Incompatibilities: Amphothericin B, Calcium chloride, Caspofungin, Cefepime, Cefotaxime, Ciprofloxacin, Dexamethasone, Diazepam, Dobutamine, Fentanyl, Fluconazole, Lorazepam, Methylprednisolone, Metronidazole, Midazolam, Milrinone, Naloxone, Phenytoin, Ranitidine, Rocuronium, Vancomycin
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Leaflet, NeoFax, Pedmed

name: Paracetamol 1000mg/100ml injection
Dose: Analgesia, neonates (IV/oral): <32 weeks 7.5mg/kg/dose TDS [Max 22.5mg/kg/day]; >32 weeks & <10 days of life 7.5mg/kg/dose QID [Max 30mg/kg/day]; >32 weeks & >10 days of life 15mg/kg/dose QID [Max 60mg/kg/day]. Infants & children 15mg/kg/dose QID [Max 1g/dose]. PDA closure: IV/PO 15mg/kg/dose QID for 3-7 days.
Incompatibilities: Diazepam, lipids
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Leaflet, NeoFax, KEMH

name: Phenobarbitone 200mg/ml injection
Dose: Status epilepticus loading (IV): 20mg/kg [Max 1g] over 20-30 minutes; may repeat 10-20mg/kg 5-10 minutes after the initial dose if haemodynamically stable, to a cumulative 40mg/kg. Maintenance (IV/oral): 2-10mg/kg/day in 1-2 divided doses, starting 12-24 hours after loading [Max 400mg/day]. Unit practice: 2mg/kg ON. Hepatobiliary scintigraphy (5 days before HIDA scan): 5mg/kg/day in 1-2 divided doses (oral).
Incompatibilities: Lipids, Hydrocortisone succinate, Insulin, Ranitidine, Vancomycin
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Leaflet, NeoFax, ANMF, Paed Protocol

name: Phenytoin Sodium 250mg/5ml injection
Dose: Loading (IV): 20mg/kg [Max 1.25g] diluted in NS (max 10mg/ml), infuse over 20-30 minutes with cardiac monitoring. Maintenance (IV/oral): preterm 2mg/kg BD; 1st week of life 3mg/kg BD; >1 week-4 years 3mg/kg TDS. TDM required. Do NOT dilute with D5% (precipitation).
Incompatibilities: Amikacin, Cefepime, Ceftazidime, Clindamycin, Dobutamine, Fentanyl, Heparin, Hydrocortisone, Insulin, Lidocaine, Linezolid, Methadone, Micafungin, Morphine, Phenobarbitone, Potassium chloride, Propofol, Sodium bicarbonate, Vitamin K
Method of administration: IV infusion over 30 minutes, max rate 1-3mg/kg/min
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Leaflet, UpToDate

name: Phosphate Sandoz effervescent tablet (oral)
Dose: Maintenance 1-2mmol/kg/day in divided doses. Neonate: dissolve 1 tablet in 10mL water, draw (weight(kg) x 10 / 16) mL [= 1mmol/kg/day; x1.5 for 1.5mmol/kg/day], further dilute to 8mL (3-hourly feeds) or 12mL (2-hourly feeds) and give 1mL per feed. 1 tablet = 16.1mmol PO4, 3.1mmol K, 20.4mmol Na. >2mmol/kg/day commonly causes GI upset. Stable 24h after dilution at room temperature.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Dissolve tablet in water per unit dilution protocol before dosing
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: SGH formulary

name: Polymyxin B 500,000 unit (Lyophilized) injection
Dose: Severe, life-threatening, multidrug-resistant infection: IV 20,000 units/kg/dose 12 hourly. Renal adjusted: CrCl>20mL/min 15,000u/kg 12h; CrCl5-20mL/min 10,000u/kg 12h; CrCl<5mL/min 3,000u/kg 12h.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Reconstitute with 5mL WFI to become 500,000 unit/5mL. Withdraw required dose, further dilute with D5% to 1000 unit/mL for administration.
Incompatibilities: Neomycin, Gentamicin, Amikacin, Colistin, Heparin
Method of administration: IV infusion over 60-90 minutes; can infuse over 3 hours if volume is large
Ref: Leaflet, UpToDate, Micromedex

name: Potassium chloride 10% (1g/10ml) injection
Dose: Fast correction - peripheral: 0.15mL/kg/hr for 3 hours (0.2mmol/kg/hr, ≤10mmol/hr), dilute 1:15 with NS/D5% (max 0.1mmol/mL). Central: 0.3mL/kg/hr for 1-2 hours (0.4mmol/kg/hr, ≤20mmol/hr), dilute 1:5 (max 0.4mmol/mL). Maintenance 2-4mmol/kg/day [Max 20mmol/dose]. Deficit (mmol) = (target K - current K) x 0.4 x weight. 1mL = 1.34mmol K. Must be diluted, by infusion, with cardiac monitoring.
Incompatibilities: Amphotericin B, Diazepam, Phenytoin, lipid, Amoxicillin, Azithromycin, Methylprednisolone, Suxamethonium, Thiopental
Method of administration: IV infusion over 1 hour, DO NOT administer undiluted
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Leaflet, ANMF

name: Potassium chloride 1g/10ml oral solution
Dose: Maintenance: 1.5-3mL/kg/day (2-4mmol/kg/day) in divided doses [Max 20mmol/dose]. Deficit (mmol) = (target K - current K) x 0.4 x weight [do not exceed 50mmol/day]. 1mL = 1.34mmol K.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Reconstitute powder with WFI per product; shake well before use
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: UpToDate, RCH Melbourne, SGH formulary

name: Potassium dihydrogen phosphate injection (1mmol/mL)
Dose: Correction: 0.36mL/kg (0.36mmol/kg) over 6 hours, max 0.2mL/kg/hr [Max 10mmol per correction]. Must be diluted: peripheral 1:25 to 1:50 with NS/D5% (max 0.05mmol/mL); central 1:10 (max 0.12mmol/mL). Cardiac monitoring. 1mL = 1mmol K + 1mmol PO4.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026

name: Rocuronium 50mg/5ml injection
Dose: 0.6-1.2mg/kg IV stat. Infusion 5-15mcg/kg/min (0.3-0.9mg/kg/hr).
Incompatibilities: Amphotericin, Amoxicillin, Azathioprine, Cefazolin, Cloxacillin, Dexamethasone, Diazepam, Erythromycin, Frusemide, Hydrocortisone, Insulin, Lipids, Methylprednisolone, Micafungin, Prednisolone, Thiopental, Trimethoprim, Vancomycin
Ref: Leaflet, Neofax

name: Salbutamol 500mcg/1ml injection
Dose: IV (MGH): loading 5-10mcg/kg over 10 minutes; maintenance 1-5mcg/kg/minute. Dilution ≤8kg: 1.5mg/kg in 25ml NS (1ml/hr = 1mcg/kg/min). Nebulised for hyperkalaemia: 2.5-5mg (0.5-1ml of 0.5%) - see Hyperkalaemia tab. Other (not in MGH guide): IV for hyperkalaemia 4mcg/kg over 5 min.
Incompatibilities: Pantoprazole
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: NeoMed, KEMH, Leeds Teaching Hospitals, Paediatric Protocols 4th Ed

name: Sildenafil 10mg/ml oral suspension
Dose: Persistent pulmonary hypertension: start PO 0.5mg/kg 6-8 hourly; may titrate up to 2mg/kg 6-8 hourly by clinical response (up to 3mg/kg 6 hourly reported short-term in neonates). Discontinue after 6-8 doses if no improvement. See PPHN tab.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Commercial oral suspension; shake well before use
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: NeoFax 2020, PP5, ANMF

name: Sodium benzoate 2g/10ml injection
Dose: Hyperammonaemia, body weight ≤20kg: loading 250mg/kg over 90-120 minutes, then 250mg/kg/day over 24 hours. Mixed with L-arginine and sodium phenylbutyrate in D10% total 50ml (max 50mg/ml).
Incompatibilities: Single line, only mixable with sodium phenylbutyrate & L-arginine
Method of administration: IV infusion via large vein/central line
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: NeoFax, Paeds Protocol

name: Sodium bicarbonate 8.4% w/v injection
Dose: Metabolic acidosis - volume of 4.2% (mL): full correction = [0.3 x BE x weight(kg)] x 2; half correction = [0.3 x BE x weight x 0.5] x 2. If BE not available (emergency): 1mmol/kg/dose [Max 50mmol]; repeat guided by blood gas. Dilute 8.4% 1:1 with WFI to 4.2% before infusion. Discuss with specialist before starting (rebound alkalosis, hypokalaemia, hypocalcaemia, worsening intracellular acidosis).
Incompatibilities: Adrenaline, amiodarone, amphothericin B, calcium, cefotaxime, magnesium and phosphate infusions, dobutamine, dopamine, ganciclovir, imipenem-cilastatin, lipid, midazolam, vancomycin, thiopentone, noradrenaline, PN
Method of administration: IV infusion over 30-60 minutes or continuous infusion; avoid simultaneous administration with catecholamines via same line
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Leaflet, NeoFax, South Australian Neonatal Medication Guidelines, Leeds Teaching Hospital NHS Trust

name: Sodium chloride 1g/10mL mixture (10%) (oral)
Dose: Maintenance 1.2-3.5mL/kg/day (2-6mmol/kg/day) in divided doses. Deficit (mmol) = (target Na - current Na) x 0.6 (male) or 0.5 (female) x weight; mL = mmol / 1.71. 1mL = 1.71mmol Na.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026

name: Sodium chloride 3% w/v for intravenous infusion
Dose: Content per 1000mL: Sodium 513mmol/L, Chloride 513mmol/L. Osmolarity 1026 mosm/L.

name: Sodium citrate 500mg + citric acid 334mg/5mL mixture (Shohl's solution)
Dose: Metabolic acidosis: start 1mmol/kg/day bicarbonate, titrate to target serum bicarbonate. Distal (type 1) RTA: 2-4mmol/kg/day in divided doses, up to 4-8mmol/kg/day. Proximal (type 2) RTA: 10-15mmol/kg/day, up to 20mmol/kg/day. 1mL = 1mmol Na = 1mmol HCO3. Prescribe in mL.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026

name: Sodium glycerophosphate (Glycophos) 20mmol/20ml injection
Dose: Correction: 0.36mL/kg (0.36mmol/kg) over 6-10 hours, max 0.2mL/kg/hr [Max 20-40mmol per correction]. Maintenance 1-2mmol/kg/day. 1mL = 1mmol PO4 + 2mmol Na. Dilute with WFI (preferred; NS if hyponatraemic): peripheral 1:3 (max 0.33mmol/mL), central 1:2.5 (max 0.4mmol/mL).
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Dilute in WFI or NS; peripheral line max concentration 0.1mmol/mL, central line max 0.4mmol/mL
Incompatibilities: Solutions containing magnesium or calcium (e.g. Hartmann's, Ringer's, Plasmalyte), TPN
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: NeoFax, SGH formulary

name: Sodium phenylbutyrate 2g/10ml injection
Dose: Hyperammonaemia, body weight ≤20kg: loading 250mg/kg over 90-120 minutes, then 250mg/kg/day over 24 hours. Mixed with L-arginine and sodium benzoate in D10% total 50ml (max 50mg/ml).
Incompatibilities: Single line, only mixable with sodium benzoate & L-arginine
Method of administration: IV infusion via large vein/central line
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: NeoFax, Paeds Protocol

name: Sodium valproate 400mg injection
Dose: Status epilepticus loading (IV): 20mg/kg [Max 1.25g] over 30 minutes. Maintenance (IV/oral): 5mg/kg/dose BD, may increase to 60mg/kg/day in 2-3 divided doses [Max 2.5g/day]. TDM required.
Incompatibilities: Phenytoin (valproate diluted in NS not compatible with phenytoin)
Method of administration: IV infusion over 60 minutes or continuous infusion
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Leaflet, Paeds Protocol, Micromedex, ANMF

name: Spironolactone 25mg tablet
Dose: Anti-failure/diuresis - NICU/SCN practice: 3.125mg/dose OD-BD (fixed dose). Infants & children: 1mg/kg BD, depending on response. For tablet, round up to nearest 6.25mg or 12.5mg/dose.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Compounded to 2.5mg/mL
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: SGH extemp formulary

name: Sucrose 24% oral solution
Dose: Procedural analgesia, 1-2 minutes before the painful procedure: preterm infants 0.5-1ml; term infants 2ml. Effective in 0-18 months only. Dilute before use: add 40ml WFI to the bottle (22.4ml Syrup BP) and shake to 62.4ml; store in fridge after dilution, stable 7 days.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Add WFI to bottle per product to reconstitute
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: NeoFax, SGH formulary

name: Sulphamethoxazole 200mg & Trimethoprim 40mg/5ml suspension (Bactrim)
Dose: CONTRAINDICATED <4 weeks of age and in G6PD deficiency; caution <2 months. Dose on TRIMETHOPRIM component. General 4mg/kg/dose BD. UTI prophylaxis 2mg/kg/dose ON. Recurrent cholangitis prophylaxis post-Kasai 4mg/kg/dose OD. PCP prophylaxis 5mg/kg/dose OD or 3 times a week; PCP treatment 15-20mg/kg/day in 3-4 divided doses.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026

name: Tazobactam & Piperacillin 4.5g (Tazocin) injection
Dose: 110mg/kg/dose, interval by PMA and days of life: PMA ≤29 weeks: ≤28 days 12 hourly, >28 days 8 hourly. PMA 30-36 weeks: ≤14 days 12 hourly, >14 days 8 hourly. PMA 37-44 weeks: ≤7 days 12 hourly, >7 days 8 hourly. PMA ≥45 weeks: 8 hourly. Infants <6 months: 110mg/kg/dose 8 hourly; ≥6 months: 110mg/kg/dose 6 hourly [Max 4.5g/dose]. Dose based on piperacillin + tazobactam (8:1).
Incompatibilities: Aminoglycosides, acyclovir, albumin, amiodarone, azithromycin, caspofungin, chlorpromazine, ciprofloxacin, dobutamine, ganciclovir, glycopyrronium bromide, hydralazine, insulin (short-acting), midazolam, pentamidine isetionate, rocuronium, sodium bicarbonate, thiopentone, tranexamic acid, verapamil
Method of administration: IV infusion over at least 60 minutes
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Leaflet, Neofax, Neomed, NAG 2024

name: Thiamine HCl 200mg/2mL injection
Dose: Refeeding syndrome / prevention or treatment of vitamin B1 deficiency: IV/PO 1-2mg/kg OD for 3 days (may extend up to 2 weeks) [Max 100-200mg/day].
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026

name: Thiopentone 500mg injection
Dose: Resistant seizures/status epilepticus: Loading <1mo 2mg/kg; >1mo 4mg/kg. Continuous infusion 1mg/kg/hr, max 8mg/kg/hr.
Incompatibilities: Adrenaline, Amiodarone, Azithromycin, Calcium gluconate, Dobutamine, Dopamine, Ertapenem, Frusemide, Ketamine, Leucovorin calcium, Lidocaine, Magnesium, Morphine, Midazolam, Naloxone, Noradrenaline, Tazocin, Rocuronium, Sodium bicarbonate
Method of administration: Via central route only; loading over 10-15 seconds; continuous infusion
Ref: IBM compatibility, South Australian Neonatal Medication Guideline

name: Tobramycin injection
Dose: Gram-negative infection (alternative aminoglycoside): dosing similar structure to Gentamicin — 4-5mg/kg/dose, extended-interval by current PMA (see Gentamicin entry/Sepsis tab pattern as a guide). Confirm local frequency chart before use — less commonly stocked than gentamicin/amikacin at this unit.
Ref: NeoFax 2020 (general aminoglycoside dosing pattern)

name: Tranexamic acid 500mg/5ml injection
Dose: Major bleeding/haemorrhage: 10-15 mg/kg/dose IV, 8 hourly.
Method of administration: Slow IV over 5-10 minutes — do not exceed 1mL/min (hypotension risk if too fast)
Ref: SGH formulary

name: Trimethoprim 80mg & Sulfamethoxazole 400mg (Co-trimoxazole/ Bactrim) injection
Dose: CONTRAINDICATED <4 weeks of age and in G6PD deficiency; caution <2 months. Dose based on trimethoprim (TMP) component. General: 4mg/kg/dose BD. PCP treatment: 15-20mg/kg/day in 3-4 divided doses. Melioidosis: 4-6mg/kg/dose BD.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Take required dose and further dilute to 15 times (fluid restriction, central line only) or 25 times.
Storage after reconstitution: 6 hours at RT, DO NOT refrigerate
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Leaflet, UpToDate, Micromedex

name: Ursodeoxycholic acid 250mg capsule
Dose: Neonatal cholestasis: 10-15mg/kg/dose BD. Infants & children: 5-10mg/kg/dose BD.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Compounded to 50mg/mL
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: ANMF

name: Valganciclovir 50mg/ml oral syrup
Dose: Congenital CMV infection treatment (step-down from IV ganciclovir, or primary oral treatment): 16 mg/kg/dose PO q12h for 6 months total. CYTOTOXIC drug.
Reconstitution/ dilution/ special instru: Commercial or CDR-pharmacy compounded; requires ≥1 day advance notice; shake well before use
Ref: UpToDate, SGH formulary

name: Vancomycin 500mg injection
Dose: Neonates: PMA <29 weeks 15mg/kg/dose 24 hourly; PMA 29-35 weeks 15mg/kg/dose 12 hourly; PMA >35 weeks 15mg/kg/dose 8 hourly. Infants & children: 15-20mg/kg/dose 8 hourly. Severe infection: 25-30mg/kg loading, then 15mg/kg/dose 6-8 hourly [Max 3g/day]. TDM required. Oral (C. difficile): 10mg/kg/dose QID [Max 125mg/dose non-severe] - no TDM needed for oral.
Incompatibilities: Cefazolin, Cefepime, Cefotaxime, Cefoxitin, Ceftazidime, Ceftriaxone, Dexamethasone, Heparin >1u/ml, Phenobarbitone, Tazocin
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: Leaflet, NeoFax

name: Varicella zoster immunoglobulin 125 IU vial (Varitect CP)
Dose: Varicella post-exposure prophylaxis: 25 IU/kg IV single dose (Varitect CP).
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026

name: Vasopressin 20 iu/1ml injection
Dose: Hypotension: 0.5unit/kg in 50ml (1ml/hr=0.01unit/kg/hr), range 0.01-0.04 units/kg/hr, titrate q20min. Refractory PPHN: 0.3unit/kg in 50ml (1ml/hr=0.006unit/kg/hr), up to max 0.072unit/kg/hr. DI: starting 0.5mU/kg/hr, usual 0.5-2mU/kg/hr up to 3mU/kg/hr. If serum Na<140, stop vasopressin.
Incompatibilities: Amphoterin B, Diazepam, Frusemide, Phenytoin
Ref: Leaflet, UpToDate, ANMF

name: Vitamin A oral/IM injection
Dose: Vitamin A deficiency / measles treatment (MGH, oral vitamin A acetate powder): <6 months 50,000 IU single dose on Day 1; repeat on Day 2 and 14 if signs of deficiency (e.g. corneal ulceration) or measles. 100,000 IU = 0.3g; dilute 1 pack (0.3g) in 5mL water. Other (not in MGH guide): BPD-prevention regimens - confirm local regimen before use.
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: NeoFax, ANMF — confirm local regimen before use

name: Vitamin E (Tocopherol) oral drops
Dose: Preterm supplementation: 40 units (2 drops) OD (not weight-based).
Ref: ANMF

name: Vitamin K 1mg/1ml (Phytomenadione) injection
Dose: Prophylaxis of vitamin K deficiency bleeding - neonates: IV 0.3mg/kg OD for 3 days; IM single dose at birth: BW <1500g 0.5mg, BW ≥1500g 1mg. Infants & children: IV/PO 0.3mg/kg OD [Max 10mg]. IV: do not give as rapid infusion - dilute with NS/D5% and infuse over 30-60 minutes. Avoid the 10mg/mL strength in <2 years (benzyl alcohol). Other (not in MGH guide): neonatal cholestasis 2mg twice weekly up to 2mg OD.
Incompatibilities: Amphotericin (conventional), ampicillin, diazepam, dobutamine, hydralazine, lipid, magnesium sulphate, methylprednisolone, phenytoin, promethazine, sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim
Method of administration: IV infusion over 1 hour (Do Not give bolus); intramuscular
Ref: MGH Paeds Dosing Guide 2026 (dose); preparation info: ANMF, leaflet

name: Zinc 15mg, B6, Vitamin A tablet
Dose: 1 mg/kg/day elemental zinc, up to 1 tablet OD. Each tablet ≈ 14.9mg elemental zinc.
Ref: SGH formulary
